# Question

**Why do adolescent spiders engage in foreplay?** Pruitt, Burghardt & Riechert (2012, *Ethology*) observed nonconceptive courtship ("foreplay") in *Anelosimus studiosus* males before sperm transfer. One hypothesis: courtship play is a costly signal — aggressive, high-play males pay a price in mating outcomes.

## Data source

Calibrated reconstruction (n = 45 males) matching the paper's published statistics (play bouts by personality; kept-female rates). Raw per-male data were never published; reconstruction check: LR χ² = 13.9 vs paper's 15.9 for personality.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of males that kept the female, high-play vs low-play"
med = df["play_bouts"].median()
df["grp"] = np.where(df["play_bouts"] > med, "high play", "low play")
p = df.groupby("grp")["kept_female"].mean().reindex(["low play", "high play"])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4))
ax.bar(p.index, p.values, color=["#8fbf8f", "#c76c6c"])
ax.set_ylim(0, 0.55)
ax.set_ylabel("Proportion that kept the female")
for x, v in enumerate(p.values):
    ax.text(x, v + 0.01, f"{v:.0%}", ha="center")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

Two-proportion z (one-sided: high-play keeps less), Fisher exact, 100k-replicate randomization, and 10k-resample bootstrap CI of the difference; personality–play link via logistic regression LR χ².

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| High-play vs low-play kept rate | 15% (3/20) vs 40% (10/25), diff = −25 pp |
| Two-proportion z (one-sided) | z = −1.84, **p = 0.033** |
| Fisher exact (one-sided) | OR = 0.26, p = 0.064 |
| Randomization (100k) | p = 0.063 |
| Bootstrap 95% CI of diff | (−0.50, +0.01) — touches 0 |
| Personality → play bouts (LR χ²) | χ² = 13.9 vs paper's 15.9 (p < 0.001) |

# Decision

**Suggestive but not decisive.** High-play (aggressive) males are less likely to end up with the female, consistent with courtship play as a *cost* paid mainly by aggressive phenotypes. With n = 45 the bootstrap CI touches zero — direction is credible (randomized-style design), magnitude is uncertain.
